summary: Register-blocking optimization of the bit-exact coopmat matmul: ONE workgroup (32 threads = 1 subgroup) computes an RB_M x RB_N BLOCK of 16x16 output tiles, holding RB_M*RB_N loop-carried coopmat accumulators in ONE K-loop, loading each A row-tile and each B col-tile from shared ONCE per K-block and REUSING across the block. This raises arithmetic intensity ~min(RB_M,RB_N)x from the M3.3b 1-tile/workgroup baseline (which is issue/bandwidth-bound, not FLOP-bound). The N-coopmat-phi codegen path is ALREADY GENERAL (verified: detect_loop_carried_coopmat collects the full SET of carried coopmats, emits N phis via parallel pre_header_values/latch_values/carried Vecs; AT-1702 proves multi-phi well-formedness across loops, and the SAME Vec machinery handles N phis in ONE loop) — NO codegen change is required for register blocking. RB_M, RB_N are genuinely-used @strategy holes (they parameterize accumulator count + shared-tile sizes + dispatch grid). Multi-subgroup blocking is DEFERRED (no LocalInvocationId/SubgroupId-within-workgroup/NumSubgroups builtin exists — confirmed by grep; adding one is out of scope for M3.3c and would be a separate language addition). STAYS BIT-EXACT; report the measured TFLOPS HONESTLY without an asserted ratio.

files_to_create.purpose: Register-blocked coopmat matmul. ONE workgroup (32 threads, 1 subgroup) computes an RB_M x RB_N block of 16x16 output tiles. RB_M*RB_N loop-carried coopmat accumulators (let mut acc_ij = coopmat_zero() for each i in 0..RB_M, j in 0..RB_N), all accumulated in ONE K-loop. Shared A tile = (RB_M*16) x 16 f16, shared B tile = 16 x (RB_N*16) f16. Per K-block: stage A block + B block to shared, barrier, coopmat_load each of the RB_M A row-tiles and each of the RB_N B col-tiles from shared (reused), then RB_M*RB_N coopmat_mul_add into the accumulators. Store all RB_M*RB_N accumulators. @strategy { rb_m, rb_n, tile_k, a_block_size, b_block_size }. tile_k FIXED at 16 (bound to coopmat K dim, same constraint as M3.3b). MUST be hand-written for FIXED small RB dims (e.g. 2x2) because AXIOM has no compile-time unrolling over a strategy hole — see open_question OQ-1 and coder_handoff_notes HN-1. The committed example is the 2x2 unrolled variant; the @strategy holes parameterize the dispatch grid + shared sizes + the bench, and the bench/autotuner select among PRE-WRITTEN unrolled variants (2x2 ships; 2x4 / 4x4 are follow-up variants noted but NOT required to ship if register pressure caps them).

technical_spec:
## M3.3c — Register-Blocked Coopmat Matmul

### 1. The bottleneck (why M3.3b is at 4%)
M3.3b's matmul_shared_coopmat.axc dispatches ONE 16x16 output tile per workgroup, ONE subgroup (32 lanes), ONE coopmat accumulator. Each K-block: stage 256 A + 256 B f16 to shared, barrier, coopmat_load A + B, ONE coopmat_mul_add, barrier. Arithmetic intensity is ~1 MMA (16x16x16 = 8192 FLOP) per (256+256) f16 shared loads + 2 coopmat_loads. The GPU is issue/bandwidth-bound, not FLOP-bound: the tensor cores idle waiting on staging + barriers. 5.04 TFLOPS = 4.0% of the 125-TFLOPS datasheet estimate.

### 2. Register blocking (the fix AXIOM CAN express)
Keep ONE workgroup = ONE subgroup (32 lanes) — but compute an RB_M x RB_N BLOCK of 16x16 output tiles instead of one. Hold RB_M*RB_N coopmat accumulators, ALL accumulated in ONE K-loop. The KEY win: in each K-block, load the RB_M A row-tiles and RB_N B col-tiles from shared ONCE, then REUSE them across the RB_M*RB_N MMAs:
```
for i in 0..RB_M:   a_mat[i] = coopmat_load(a_tile, row_off=i*16, stride=16)
for j in 0..RB_N:   b_mat[j] = coopmat_load(b_tile, col_off=j*16, stride=RB_N*16)
for i in 0..RB_M: for j in 0..RB_N: acc[i][j] = coopmat_mul_add(a_mat[i], b_mat[j], acc[i][j])
```
Now RB_M*RB_N MMAs (e.g. 4 for 2x2 = 32768 FLOP) share RB_M+RB_N coopmat_loads (4 for 2x2) and the SAME staging cost amortized over the block. Arithmetic intensity rises ~RB-fold; the tensor cores stay busier. Shared staging per K-block: A block = (RB_M*16) rows x 16 cols, B block = 16 rows x (RB_N*16) cols.

### 3. The dispatch grid shrinks
Grid = (N / (RB_N*16), M / (RB_M*16), 1) workgroups. Index recovery (SAME idiom as M3.3b, gid + integer division — NO new builtin):
- block_col = gid(0) / 32   (local_size.x=32; 32 lanes collapse to one block_col)
- block_row = gid(1)        (local_size.y=1; gid(1)==workgroup_id.y, NO division)
- lane = subgroup_invocation_id() == gid(0)%32 (coopmat lane source)
Output tile (i,j) of the block: tile_row = block_row*RB_M + i, tile_col = block_col*RB_N + j. c_base[i][j] = (tile_row*16)*N + (tile_col*16), stored with stride N. NOTE: the dispatch grid is SMALLER (fewer workgroups, more work each) — total FLOP unchanged, occupancy still ample at M=N=256 (e.g. 2x2 -> 8x8=64 workgroups, plenty for the GPU's SMs).

### 4. Shared staging (32 threads stage the RB block)
A block size = RB_M*16*16 = RB_M*256 f16 elements; B block size = 16*RB_N*16 = RB_N*256 f16 elements. With 32 threads, a_iters = a_block_size/32 = RB_M*8, b_iters = RB_N*8. Staging loops mirror M3.3b's linear-index pattern, generalized: A block row span = block_row*RB_M*16 .. +RB_M*16 global rows; B block col span = block_col*RB_N*16 .. +RB_N*16 global cols. Staging A element ei = a_iter*32+lane -> a_row = ei/16 (row in the RB_M*16-tall A block), a_col = ei - a_row*16 (the K-block column, width 16=tile_k); A global row = block_row*RB_M*16 + a_row; A global col = k_block*16 + a_col. Staging B element ei -> b_row = ei/(RB_N*16) (K-block row, height 16), b_col = ei - b_row*(RB_N*16) (col in the RB_N*16-wide B block); B global row = k_block*16 + b_row; B global col = block_col*RB_N*16 + b_col. A-tile shared stride = 16 (tile_k); B-tile shared stride = RB_N*16. coopmat_load for a_mat[i]: base offset = i*16*16 (i-th 16-row slab, stride 16). coopmat_load for b_mat[j]: base offset = j*16 (j-th 16-col band, stride RB_N*16).

### 5. N loop-carried coopmat accumulators — codegen is ALREADY general (VERIFIED)
emit_for_range (crates/axc-codegen/src/body.rs) -> detect_loop_carried_coopmat (line 932) collects the WHOLE SET of carried coopmat bindings (iterates em.coopmat_binding_ids, sorts deterministically by BindingId, pushes EACH carried one with its own pre-allocated phi_id) -> returns Vec<(BindingId, Word)>. Steps 3/5/7/10/11 use PARALLEL Vecs (pre_header_values[i], latch_values[i], carried[i]) — fully general over N. Step 10 post-inserts N OpPhis in REVERSE declaration order at the header head (so they end up in declaration order at indices 0..N, satisfying SPIR-V 2.4 'all phis first'). AT-1702 already proves the multi-phi insert is well-formed (2 phis across 2 NESTED loops); the SAME Vec machinery produces N phis in ONE loop. THEREFORE register blocking with RB_M*RB_N=4 accumulators needs NO codegen change. AT-1733 (new compile+spirv-val test) LOCKS this guarantee for N=4 in a single loop. CONSTRAINT carried over from M3.3b: each accumulator must be (a) coopmat-typed, (b) defined (coopmat_zero) BEFORE the K-loop, (c) reassigned UNCONDITIONALLY at top level in the body (no if/else reassign — AT-1708 hard error), (d) no break/continue carrying it (AT-1704). The unrolled RB body satisfies all four for every acc_ij.

### 6. Why the example is hand-unrolled (NOT a runtime RB loop)
AXIOM has NO compile-time unrolling over a @strategy hole, and the coopmat accumulators must be DISTINCT named SSA bindings (let mut acc_00, acc_01, acc_10, acc_11) for the N-phi detection to bind them — a runtime `for i in 0..RB_M` over an ARRAY of coopmats is NOT expressible (coopmats are SSA, not addressable; there is no coopmat array type). So the committed example HARD-CODES RB_M=RB_N=2 (4 named accumulators, 4 unrolled MMAs, 2+2 unrolled loads). The @strategy holes (rb_m, rb_n, a_block_size, b_block_size) are still GENUINELY USED: they drive the shared-array sizes (shared a_tile: shared[f16, ?a_block_size]) and the bench's dispatch-grid + assignment selection. To sweep RB dims the autotuner/bench selects among PRE-WRITTEN unrolled variant files (2x2 ships; 2x4/4x4 are optional follow-up variants). This is the honest expressibility boundary and is documented (OQ-1).

### 7. Register / shared pressure (the cap)
Each coopmat accumulator consumes a coopmat register-file slot (16x16 f16 accumulator distributed across the 32-lane subgroup = ~8 f16/lane per accumulator). 2x2 = 4 accumulators + the transient a_mat[0..2]/b_mat[0..2] = ~8 live coopmats — comfortably within a Blackwell warp's register file. 4x4 = 16 accumulators + 8 transient = 24 live coopmats: MAY exceed the register file and spill (collapsing throughput). The DEFAULT shipped variant is 2x2 (safe, clear uplift); 2x4 (8 acc) is the stretch variant; 4x4 is NOTED as likely register-bound — the bench/autotuner measures and the HONEST winner is reported (if 4x4 spills and 2x2 wins, that is the reported result). Shared pressure: 2x2 A block = 2*256 = 512 f16 = 1024 B; B block = 2*256 = 512 f16 = 1024 B; total 2048 B << maxComputeSharedMemorySize (>=16KB everywhere, 48-228KB on the RTX PRO 6000). 4x4 = 4*256+4*256 = 2048 f16 = 4096 B — still tiny. Shared is NOT the cap; registers are. The runtime preflight (context.rs preflight_kernel_support line 869, SharedMemoryExceedsDeviceLimit) still gates it fail-closed.

### 8. Double-buffered shared staging (software pipelining) — DEFERRED
Prefetching the next K-block into a second shared buffer while computing the current would hide staging latency further, but (a) it needs two shared buffers + a manual ping-pong index and an extra barrier discipline that the current barrier-soundness analyzer (AT-1606 cross-slot) must accept, and (b) the register-blocking uplift is the dominant, lower-risk win. DEFERRED to a follow-up; NOT in M3.3c scope. Noted in design so it is a tracked, not forgotten, option.

### 9. Multi-subgroup blocking — BLOCKED, DEFERRED (honest path b)
Multi-subgroup (multiple warps per workgroup, each warp doing a sub-block, sharing the staged A/B across the whole workgroup) needs a way for each invocation to know its SUBGROUP index within the workgroup (or its LocalInvocationId, from which subgroup id = LocalInvocationId.x / subgroup_size). GREP CONFIRMS AXIOM exposes ONLY: GlobalInvocationId (gid), SubgroupLocalInvocationId (subgroup_invocation_id), SubgroupSize (subgroup_size). There is NO LocalInvocationId, NO SubgroupId-within-workgroup, NO NumSubgroups builtin (crates/axc-hir/src/subgroup.rs + codegen emit only the two scalar subgroup builtins). Multi-subgroup blocking is therefore NOT expressible without a NEW builtin. DECISION: defer (path b). Adding local_invocation_id() (SPIR-V BuiltIn LocalInvocationId, a uvec3 Input var, lowering identical to the existing GlobalInvocationId var in buffers.rs) is a real but bounded language addition scoped to a SEPARATE milestone (M3.3d / M3.4). Rationale: register blocking alone is expected to deliver the bulk of the realistic single-subgroup uplift; bundling a new builtin + multi-warp shared-tile choreography + its barrier-soundness proof into M3.3c multiplies risk. Multi-subgroup is documented as the NEXT lever requiring the builtin.

### 10. Correctness oracle (BIT-EXACT)
max_diff == 0.0 vs cpu_f16_matmul_reference on the NON-SYMMETRIC integer-f16 fixture (A in {1..4}, B in {1..3}, per-element sum <= 2048 so f16-integer-exact). The RB block changes ONLY the loop/tiling structure, NOT the numerics: each acc_ij accumulates exactly the same sequence of coopmat_mul_add(A[tile_row_i], B[tile_col_j]) over the same K-blocks as the M3.3b single-tile kernel would for that (i,j) tile. Coopmat mul_add is the SAME tensor-core op; same K-block order -> bit-identical. AT-1731 (2x2, fixed K) + AT-1732 (2x2, K=32 vs K=48 to vary the OpPhi trip count) assert max_diff==0. The pre-existing AT-1620/1622 (single-tile) are RETAINED and must still pass.

### 11. Honesty
Report the BARE measured effective TFLOPS + % of 125. If 2x2 lifts 4% -> e.g. 10-15%, say exactly that. If register pressure caps the realistic ceiling well below 'competitive' (25%), report that honestly and label NON-competitive. NO asserted ratio (only tflops>0 && finite, AT-1730). If an RB variant spills and underperforms, the bench reports it and the winner is the honest best (possibly 2x2). If double-buffering or 4x4 are tried and do not help, the report says so.

correctness_oracle: Bit-exact: max_diff == 0.0 vs cpu_f16_matmul_reference on the non-symmetric integer-f16 fixture (A in {1..4}, B in {1..3}, per-element K-sum <= 2048 so every partial product and sum is f16-integer-exact). The RB tiling changes ONLY loop structure, not the numeric op sequence: acc_ij accumulates exactly the same ordered coopmat_mul_add(A[tile_row_i,k], B[k,tile_col_j]) over the same K-blocks as a single-tile kernel for tile (i,j). Same tensor-core op + same accumulation order => bit-identical. AT-1731/1732 assert max_diff==0; AT-1620/1622 (single-tile) retained as the unchanged baseline oracle.
edge_cases: Register pressure: 4x4 = 16 accumulators + 8 transient coopmats may exceed the warp register file and spill, collapsing throughput. SHIP 2x2 (safe); measure 2x4/4x4 and report the HONEST best — if 2x2 wins, 2x2 is the result.

Shared overflow: A block (RB_M*256 f16) + B block (RB_N*256 f16). 2x2 = 2048 B, 4x4 = 4096 B — both << maxComputeSharedMemorySize (>=16KB). The runtime preflight (SharedMemoryExceedsDeviceLimit, context.rs:869) still gates it fail-closed; AT-1734 verifies the computed shared_memory_bytes.

RB not dividing M/N: dispatch grid (N/(RB_N*16), M/(RB_M*16), 1) requires M divisible by RB_M*16 and N by RB_N*16. M3.3c restricts to those multiples (same as M3.3b's multiple-of-16 restriction, scaled by RB). Partial RB-blocks (masked/predicated coopmat load/store) are OUT OF SCOPE (carried from M3.3b edge-tile deferral).
tile_k != 16: REJECTED by the same constraint as M3.3b — one coopmat_mul_add covers exactly K=16; tile_k=16 is the only valid hole value. K-block COUNT (K/16) is the load-bearing variation.
Zero-trip K-loop (K<16): num_k_blocks = K/16 = 0 -> all acc_ij read their header phi = coopmat_zero (zero-trip-safe per the OpPhi merge). C block = 0. Fixtures use K multiple of 16, K>=16.

N coopmat phis NOT emitting correctly: GUARDED by AT-1733 (compile+spirv-val). If it fails, codegen needs a fix BEFORE the kernel ships — but the Vec-based machinery is already general, so this is expected to PASS as-is (locked, not assumed).
Conditional reassignment of an accumulator: forbidden (AT-1708 hard error). The unrolled RB body reassigns every acc_ij unconditionally at top level — satisfied by construction.

Occupancy after grid shrink: grid is RB^2 smaller (2x2 -> 64 workgroups at M=N=256). Still ample for the GPU's SMs; if a future tiny matmul under-occupies, that is a separate concern (the bench uses M=N=K=256).

open_questions.q: AXIOM cannot unroll over a @strategy hole and has no coopmat array type, so RB_M/RB_N cannot be a RUNTIME loop bound over an array of accumulators. The shipped example hard-codes 2x2 (4 named accumulators, fully unrolled). Is shipping a SINGLE hand-unrolled 2x2 variant (with the @strategy holes driving shared sizes + grid + bench, and the autotuner selecting among PRE-WRITTEN variant files) acceptable, or do reviewers want a codegen-level coopmat-array / strategy-unroll feature (a LARGER language addition) in scope? Architect recommends: ship 2x2 unrolled now; track strategy-unroll as a future language feature.

Confirm via AT-1733 that 4 coopmat phis in ONE loop emit correctly. Architect's read of detect_loop_carried_coopmat + the parallel pre_header_values/latch_values/carried Vecs + the reverse-order step-10 insert says YES (no change needed), and AT-1702 proves the multi-phi insert mechanism. Is the Pessimistic reviewer satisfied that the SINGLE-loop N-phi path (vs AT-1702's NESTED 1-phi-each) has no ordering/dominance corner case? (The step-10 reverse-insert keeps all N phis as the first instructions in the header, preserving the SPIR-V 2.4 'phis first' rule for any N.)

Multi-subgroup blocking is deferred because no LocalInvocationId/SubgroupId builtin exists. Do reviewers agree with deferring (path b) rather than adding local_invocation_id() now (path a)? Architect recommends defer: register blocking is the lower-risk high-leverage win; the builtin + multi-warp shared choreography + barrier-soundness proof is a separate milestone.

Expected uplift is bandwidth/issue-bound-amortization, not a guaranteed FLOP multiplier. If 2x2 only lifts 4% -> ~7-10% (not the optimistic ~2x), is that an acceptable M3.3c outcome (reported honestly), or should the milestone also REQUIRE the 2x4 variant be attempted to push higher? Architect recommends: ship whatever 2x2 honestly delivers + attempt 2x4 best-effort; the acceptance gate is 'IMPROVED vs 5.04', not a fixed %.

coder_handoff_notes: HN-1: matmul_rb_coopmat.axc MUST be hand-unrolled for FIXED RB_M=RB_N=2. Declare 4 named accumulators: let mut acc_00 = coopmat_zero(); ... acc_11. In the K-loop, after staging+barrier: load a_mat_0/a_mat_1 (A row-tiles, shared offsets 0 and 16*16, stride 16) and b_mat_0/b_mat_1 (B col-tiles, shared offsets 0 and 16, stride RB_N*16=32), then 4 unrolled coopmat_mul_add into acc_00/acc_01/acc_10/acc_11. Each acc_ij reassigned UNCONDITIONALLY at top level (AT-1708). After the loop, 4 unrolled coopmat_store to the 4 c_base offsets. Use explicit `return;`; no `>>` (shr/lshr).

HN-2: @strategy { rb_m: ?[2], rb_n: ?[2], tile_k: ?[16], a_block_size: ?[512], b_block_size: ?[512] }. a_block_size = RB_M*16*16 = 512; b_block_size = RB_N*16*16 = 512 (f16 element counts). shared a_tile: shared[f16, ?a_block_size]; shared b_tile: shared[f16, ?b_block_size]. These holes are GENUINELY used (shared sizes + bench grid). Document the hand-unroll boundary in the file header (OQ-1).

HN-3: NO codegen change is required — detect_loop_carried_coopmat (body.rs:932) + emit_for_range already emit N phis for N carried coopmats in one loop (verified: parallel pre_header_values/latch_values/carried Vecs, reverse-order step-10 insert). If AT-1733 FAILS, STOP and escalate to the Architect (a codegen gap, not a Coder workaround). DO NOT silently mutate body.rs to make it pass.

HN-4: Index recovery mirrors M3.3b: block_col = gid(0)/32, block_row = gid(1), lane = subgroup_invocation_id(). Output tile (i,j): tile_row = block_row*2 + i, tile_col = block_col*2 + j. c_base_ij = (tile_row*16)*N + (tile_col*16), store stride N.

### 3.1.17 M3.3c — register-blocked coopmat matmul (bit-exact + measured TFLOPS uplift)

M3.3b (§3.1.16) shipped a bit-exact multi-tile coopmat matmul at 5.04 TFLOPS = 4.0% of the 125-TFLOPS f32 datasheet estimate (NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell). The bottleneck is arithmetic intensity: ONE workgroup = ONE 16x16 output tile = ONE subgroup = ONE coopmat accumulator, so the tensor cores idle on shared staging + barriers (issue/bandwidth-bound, not FLOP-bound).

**Register blocking (matmul_rb_coopmat.axc).** Keep ONE workgroup = ONE subgroup (32 lanes), but compute an RB_M x RB_N BLOCK of 16x16 output tiles, holding RB_M*RB_N loop-carried coopmat accumulators in ONE K-loop. The win: each K-block loads RB_M A row-tiles + RB_N B col-tiles from shared ONCE and REUSES them across the RB_M*RB_N MMAs (acc[i][j] += A[i]*B[j]), raising arithmetic intensity ~RB-fold. Dispatch grid shrinks to (N/(RB_N*16), M/(RB_M*16), 1); index recovery is the SAME gid + integer-division idiom as M3.3b (block_col=gid(0)/32, block_row=gid(1), lane=subgroup_invocation_id()) — NO new builtin, NO new capability.

**N loop-carried coopmat accumulators — no codegen change.** detect_loop_carried_coopmat (body.rs) collects the WHOLE SET of carried coopmat bindings and emits N OpPhis in ONE loop header via parallel pre_header_values/latch_values/carried Vecs (reverse-order step-10 insert keeps all N phis first per SPIR-V 2.4). AT-1702 proved the multi-phi insert mechanism (2 phis across 2 nested loops); AT-1733 (new) LOCKS N=4 phis in ONE loop. Register blocking therefore needs NO codegen change. Each accumulator must be coopmat-typed, zero-initialized before the loop, and reassigned UNCONDITIONALLY at top level (AT-1708), with no break/continue (AT-1704) — the unrolled body satisfies all four.

**Hand-unrolled, not a runtime RB loop.** AXIOM has no compile-time unroll over a @strategy hole and no coopmat array type (coopmats are SSA, not addressable), so the shipped example HARD-CODES RB_M=RB_N=2 (4 named accumulators, fully unrolled). The @strategy holes (rb_m, rb_n, a_block_size, b_block_size) genuinely drive the shared-tile sizes + the bench dispatch grid; sweeping RB dims selects among PRE-WRITTEN unrolled variant files. This is the honest expressibility boundary; a strategy-unroll / coopmat-array language feature is future work.

**Bit-exact (AT-1731/1732).** Non-symmetric integer-f16 fixture (A in {1..4}, B in {1..3}, K-sum <= 2048, f16-integer-exact). RB tiling changes ONLY loop structure, not the numeric op sequence: each acc_ij accumulates the SAME ordered coopmat_mul_add over the SAME K-blocks as a single-tile kernel for tile (i,j) -> bit-identical. AT-1731 (2x2, K=32, max_diff==0) + AT-1732 (2x2, K=32 vs K=48, max_diff==0). The single-tile AT-1620/1622 are RETAINED unchanged. Typed-skip on Lavapipe (CoopMatUnsupported); matmul_shared_f32.axc remains the Lavapipe scalar path.

**Measured TFLOPS (AT-1730).** resident_matmul_rb.rs, same resident upload-once/N_WARMUP=2/MIN-of-10/GpuTimestamp methodology, M=N=K=256, grid (N/32,M/32,1). Reports the BARE effective_tflops + % of the 125-TFLOPS estimate HONESTLY; NO ratio asserted (only tflops>0 && finite); 'competitive' label ONLY if pct>=25.0. [MEASURED RESULT FILLED IN BY QA after GPU run — bare number + % HONESTLY; if register pressure caps it below 25%, labeled non-competitive.] Register pressure is the cap: 2x2 (4 acc + ~4 transient coopmats) is safe; 4x4 (16 acc) may spill the warp register file (collapsing throughput) — the bench measures and the HONEST best wins. Shared is NOT the cap (2x2 = 2048 B, 4x4 = 4096 B, both << maxComputeSharedMemorySize).

**Deferred (follow-up M3.3d / M3.4).** (1) Multi-subgroup blocking (multiple warps per workgroup sharing the staged A/B) needs a LocalInvocationId / SubgroupId-within-workgroup builtin — AXIOM exposes only GlobalInvocationId + SubgroupLocalInvocationId + SubgroupSize (grep-confirmed). Adding local_invocation_id() (SPIR-V BuiltIn LocalInvocationId, lowering identical to the existing GlobalInvocationId Input var) is a bounded but separate language addition, deferred to keep M3.3c low-risk. (2) Double-buffered shared staging (software pipelining the next K-block) — higher complexity, dominant win is register blocking, deferred. (3) Partial RB-blocks / edge tiles (M,N not multiples of RB*16) — masked/predicated coopmat load/store, carried from M3.3b.
